checks.fix: Check the engine binding (`axiom-encode engine-bind`), the `AXIOM_RULES_ENGINE_*` environment and the runner; retry the validation without changing the RuleSpec.
checks.requires: The pinned Axiom rules engine runs and returns a result.
checks.title: Axiom rules engine could not be run
checks.why: When the engine itself fails (missing binary, timeout, crash), the artifact was not judged; the failure is not the encoder output's.

checks.fix: Read the engine message (found) and fix the named rule, field or expression at the reported line; then recompile. Do not work around the error by deleting rules the source requires.
checks.requires: The RuleSpec module compiles with the pinned Axiom rules engine.
checks.title: Axiom rules engine rejected the RuleSpec
checks.why: Nothing downstream (tests, grounding, apply) can run on a module that does not compile; the engine message names the first error.

checks.fix: Keep the cited branch in the deferral output path, as in the expected value; the reason can stay.
checks.requires: Each `module.deferred_outputs` entry names its source branch by the canonical source anchor and a reason that names the exact missing dependency, input or runtime capability.
checks.title: Deferral output is rooted at the source unit, not at its branch
checks.why: A deferral is a recorded gap in the encoding. A gap that is vague, or rooted at the wrong place, cannot be audited or closed later, and it can hide law that the module should encode.

checks.fix: Remove the deferral. Declare the source-stated operative facts as local RuleSpec inputs and encode the principal derived output.
checks.requires: A branch that states an explicit computation is encoded, not deferred as a runtime gap.
checks.title: Deferral cites a branch that states an explicit computation
checks.why: The source gives everything needed to compute the branch, so a deferral drops law the encoder can encode.

checks.fix: Rewrite `module.deferred_outputs[N].output` to the canonical source anchor shown as expected, keeping the `#<output>` fragment.
checks.requires: Each `module.deferred_outputs` entry names its source branch by the canonical source anchor and a reason that names the exact missing dependency, input or runtime capability.
checks.title: Deferral output uses a non-source root
checks.why: A deferral is a recorded gap in the encoding. A gap that is vague, or rooted at the wrong place, cannot be audited or closed later, and it can hide law that the module should encode.

checks.fix: Name the exact missing dependency (a citation of the provision that is not yet encoded), input or runtime capability in the deferral `reason`, or encode the branch instead.
checks.requires: Each `module.deferred_outputs` entry names its source branch by the canonical source anchor and a reason that names the exact missing dependency, input or runtime capability.
checks.title: Deferral reason does not name an exact missing dependency
checks.why: A deferral is a recorded gap in the encoding. A gap that is vague, or rooted at the wrong place, cannot be audited or closed later, and it can hide law that the module should encode.

checks.fix: Add a principal derived rule whose formula implements the branch and whose source or formula proof cites the branch, or precisely defer the branch.
checks.requires: Each source branch that states a computation is implemented by a principal `derived` or `derived_relation` rule bound to that branch.
checks.title: Explicit source computation has no principal output
checks.why: A computation stated only as parameters cannot be executed or tested; consumers of the module get no computed amount.

checks.fix: Encode the control inside a principal derived rule that covers its branch, or precisely defer the branch.
checks.requires: Each source-stated control (a condition, limit or selection) is implemented by a principal `derived` or `derived_relation` rule that covers the control's branch.
checks.title: Source-stated control has no principal output
checks.why: A control encoded only as a parameter does not change any computed result, so the module ignores a condition the law imposes.

checks.fix: Add the principal derived output that computes the source-stated amount from its inputs and parameters.
checks.requires: A source unit that states an explicit computation has at least one principal `derived` or `derived_relation` output.
checks.title: Source unit states a computation but has no principal output
checks.why: A parameter-only module cannot compute what the source states.

checks.fix: Add a parameter (or bind the value in an existing one) for the missing value, grounded in the source text. `module.summary` does not count.
checks.requires: Every numeric value in the authoritative source text is represented by a named scalar (a parameter or a named constant) in the module.
checks.title: Source numeric value has no named scalar
checks.why: A number the source states but the module does not name is either dropped law or hidden inside a formula, where it cannot be grounded or updated.

checks.fix: Declare each source-stated fact as its own document-root `inputs` entry (a sibling of `module` and `rules`) or canonical import, combine them in a derived Judgment with formula proof, and test each gate.
checks.requires: Each factual gate that the formula's own source clause states is a distinct local input or canonical import, combined in a source-proved derived Judgment.
checks.title: Source-stated conjunctive gates collapsed into too few inputs
checks.why: An aggregate input that stands for several source-stated facts hides the conditions from tests and from callers, so a wrong answer on one gate cannot be seen.

checks.fix: Encode the branch in a rule that cites it (source path or proof excerpt from its own text), or add a precise `module.deferred_outputs` entry for that branch. Descendant citations do not cover a substantive parent chapeau.
checks.requires: Every operative branch of the authoritative source unit is cited by a rule's `source:` or proof atom, or is listed in `module.deferred_outputs` with a reason that names the exact missing dependency.
checks.title: Source branch neither encoded nor precisely deferred
checks.why: A complete-source encoding claims the whole unit. A branch that is neither encoded nor deferred is silently dropped law: the module computes a result the source does not support.

checks.fix: Add cases at each listed boundary value (and just across it) that assert the affected principal output.
checks.requires: Every source-stated boundary value is exercised by a companion case.
checks.title: Source-stated boundary input is not exercised
checks.why: Companion tests are the executed evidence that the encoding behaves as the source says. A source-stated output, branch, boundary, exception or rounding rule without a test can be wrong without any gate noticing.

checks.fix: For each listed condition, add two same-period cases that differ only in its controlling input: one where it applies and one where it blocks.
checks.requires: Each source-stated exception or applicability condition has a same-period pair of cases that differ in exactly the controlling input and assert the affected principal output.
checks.title: Source exception or condition has no positive/blocking case pair
checks.why: Companion tests are the executed evidence that the encoding behaves as the source says. A source-stated output, branch, boundary, exception or rounding rule without a test can be wrong without any gate noticing.

checks.fix: Add a companion case whose inputs select the named branch and whose asserted output depends on the branch's computation, in a period the branch's formula version covers.
checks.requires: Each source formula branch has distinct executed test evidence that reaches the branch's computation.
checks.title: Formula branch has no executed companion evidence
checks.why: Companion tests are the executed evidence that the encoding behaves as the source says. A source-stated output, branch, boundary, exception or rounding rule without a test can be wrong without any gate noticing.

checks.fix: Remove the principal output from the case's `input` and assert it under `output` instead; supply the facts it is computed from.
checks.requires: Companion cases compute and assert local principal outputs; they never supply them as inputs.
checks.title: Companion case supplies a principal output as an input
checks.why: Companion tests are the executed evidence that the encoding behaves as the source says. A source-stated output, branch, boundary, exception or rounding rule without a test can be wrong without any gate noticing.

checks.fix: Add a case with the clamped input below zero that asserts the clamped rule (and the downstream principal output when one exists). A zero input does not exercise the clamp.
checks.requires: Each direct `max(0, input)` clamp has an executed companion case with the input below zero in every distinct temporal owner context.
checks.title: Nonnegative clamp has no below-zero companion case
checks.why: Companion tests are the executed evidence that the encoding behaves as the source says. A source-stated output, branch, boundary, exception or rounding rule without a test can be wrong without any gate noticing.

checks.fix: Write the companion `.test.yaml` cases for the module.
checks.requires: A complete source-unit encoding ships a companion test suite covering outputs, branches, boundaries, exceptions and rounding rules.
checks.title: Complete source unit has no companion test suite
checks.why: Companion tests are the executed evidence that the encoding behaves as the source says. A source-stated output, branch, boundary, exception or rounding rule without a test can be wrong without any gate noticing.

checks.fix: Encode the non-applicability as a principal Judgment output and add a case that asserts it is false.
checks.requires: Unconditional source-stated non-applicability is a source-bound principal Judgment output that executes to false and is asserted false.
checks.title: Unconditional non-applicability is not witnessed
checks.why: Companion tests are the executed evidence that the encoding behaves as the source says. A source-stated output, branch, boundary, exception or rounding rule without a test can be wrong without any gate noticing.

checks.fix: Add a companion case whose `output` asserts the named principal output.
checks.requires: Every principal output is asserted by at least one companion case.
checks.title: Principal output is never asserted
checks.why: Companion tests are the executed evidence that the encoding behaves as the source says. A source-stated output, branch, boundary, exception or rounding rule without a test can be wrong without any gate noticing.

checks.fix: Apply the stated rounding (direction and unit) in the principal formula that computes the rounded amount.
checks.requires: Every source-stated rounding rule is applied in the principal formula.
checks.title: Source-stated rounding rule is absent from the principal formula
checks.why: Companion tests are the executed evidence that the encoding behaves as the source says. A source-stated output, branch, boundary, exception or rounding rule without a test can be wrong without any gate noticing.

checks.fix: Add same-period paired cases that drive the pre-rounding amount to a fraction on each side of the rounding point, asserting the unrounded intermediate and the rounded output; or precisely defer the branch when its inputs are not available.
checks.requires: Every source-stated rounding rule is demonstrated by companion cases with distinct fractional inputs on the affected principal output.
checks.title: Source-stated rounding rule has no fractional companion evidence
checks.why: Companion tests are the executed evidence that the encoding behaves as the source says. A source-stated output, branch, boundary, exception or rounding rule without a test can be wrong without any gate noticing.

checks.fix: Check the RuleSpec repo's toolchain pin and the axiom-corpus ref: the corpus checkout must include the signed release provenance and its locks or provisions. Retry after the release is published.
checks.requires: The RuleSpec toolchain pins exactly one signed corpus release, and the pinned corpus checkout carries its signed provenance.
checks.title: The pinned corpus release cannot be fetched or verified
checks.why: Encoding reads source text only from the signed release; without it the run has no authenticated source.

checks.fix: Point `repair_run_id` at the failed run whose candidate you replay, and reduce the dispatch to the shape the message names.
checks.requires: A repair replay names a different decimal workflow run and stays within the reviewed replay limits (targets, dependents, bundles).
checks.title: Repair replay inputs are outside the trusted shape
checks.why: The workflow refuses a dispatch whose inputs it cannot bind to one exact, authenticated transaction. Nothing was encoded, so the encoder output is not at fault and a retry with the same inputs fails the same way.

checks.fix: Split the dispatch into separate runs as the message says (for example merge legacy replacements first), or drop the conflicting input.
checks.requires: One dispatch is one atomic transaction: source bundles, imports, legacy or dependent migrations and queue authorization combine only in the reviewed ways.
checks.title: Source inputs mix transaction modes
checks.why: The workflow refuses a dispatch whose inputs it cannot bind to one exact, authenticated transaction. Nothing was encoded, so the encoder output is not at fault and a retry with the same inputs fails the same way.

checks.fix: Dispatch queue items only through the queue dispatcher; for a manual run, leave the queue inputs empty and pass a routable country.
checks.requires: The country is routable, and a queue target comes from an authenticated dispatcher on its first run attempt.
checks.title: Dispatch routing or queue inputs are invalid
checks.why: The workflow refuses a dispatch whose inputs it cannot bind to one exact, authenticated transaction. Nothing was encoded, so the encoder output is not at fault and a retry with the same inputs fails the same way.

checks.fix: Pass full 40-character lowercase commit SHAs for the named ref input (not a branch or a short SHA) and re-dispatch.
checks.requires: Every pinned checkout ref is a full lowercase commit SHA, and the checkout resolves to exactly that commit.
checks.title: A checkout is not pinned to the requested commit
checks.why: Signed provenance names exact commits. A branch name or a moved ref would sign work against code nobody reviewed.

checks.fix: Copy a short contiguous excerpt verbatim from the cited provision (no ellipsis, paraphrase or joined fragments), or cite the provision that holds the text.
checks.requires: Each proof atom `source.excerpt` / `source.quote` is a contiguous verbatim span of the provision named by its `corpus_citation_path`.
checks.title: Proof excerpt does not appear in the cited provision
checks.why: A proof atom ties a rule to the exact source words it implements. An excerpt that is not in the cited provision, or not in the rule's own subsection, proves nothing and can hide an invented value or condition.

checks.fix: Take the excerpt from inside the rule's declared subsection, or correct the rule's `source` to the subsection the excerpt is from.
checks.requires: A proof excerpt that starts with a subsection marker lies inside the subsection scope of the rule's own `source`.
checks.title: Proof excerpt lies outside the rule's declared subsection
checks.why: A proof atom ties a rule to the exact source words it implements. An excerpt that is not in the cited provision, or not in the rule's own subsection, proves nothing and can hide an invented value or condition.
